children: traded at $1,283.09, down 6.9%, at 12:05 p.m. ET Thursday, leaving a wide gap between its share price and Mizuho's $2,050 target. That target implies roughly 59.8% upside. According to Investing.com, the brokerage retained its Outperform rating ahead of October 29 earnings. The bullish call sets a high bar: Sandisk needs results that give investors a reason to look beyond the selloff.

Mizuho's thesis rests on tight NAND supply and rising demand for enterprise solid-state drives, which it expects to support pricing into 2027. The immediate test is already clear. As reported by Aju Press, Sandisk projected fiscal-first-quarter revenue of $10.3 billion to $10.8 billion, adjusted earnings of $44 to $46 per share and gross margin of 83% to 85%. The revenue midpoint implies approximately 17.6% growth from the preceding quarter's $8.97 billion. Strong demand matters. Turning it into profitable sales matters more.

The GuruFocus snapshot adds a caution flag: a GF Score of 45/100 sits alongside strong growth and financial-strength readings, showing that those strengths do not translate into a strong overall score. A displayed price-to-earnings ratio of 17.6 alone cannot settle the valuation question when memory profits can swing sharply. Investors should watch realized pricing, customer mix and the next-quarter margin outlook. The key question is how much of today's exceptional profitability Sandisk can sustain.

title: Sandisk Stocks Sink 6.9% Despite Mizuho's $2,050 AI-Storage Target
